en: (Sdp 120) Oṃ, homage to the glorious Vajrasattva!
Thus have I heard: at one time the Blessed One was dwelling in the Nandavana grove, the most excellent of all divine forests.

It was adorned with various flowers— such as *maṇi*, gold, branches, creepers, trees, shrubs, herbs, lotuses, blue water-lilies, *karṇikāra*, *bakula*, *tilaka*, *aśoka*, *māndārava*, and *mahāmāndārava*—
and was beautified by wish-fulfilling trees (*kalpavṛkṣa*) and decorated with various ornaments.
It resounded with the warbling of flocks of various birds;
it echoed with the sounds of musical instruments such as the *tūrya*, *mukunda*, flute, and drum;
and it was graced by the playful sports of Śakra, Brahmā, and other gods and apsarases of many kinds.
It was empowered by all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas;

it was attended by hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of assemblies of Śakra, Brahmā, and other gods, vidyādharas, devas, and apsarases; and by various assemblies of many hundreds of thousands of millions of great bodhisattvas, including yakṣas, rākṣasas, asuras, garuḍas, gandharvas, kinnaras, mahoragas, nāgas, and others.
They were as follows:
the bodhisattva mahāsattva Pratibhānamati and the bodhisattva mahāsattva Acalamati.
And with Vipulamati, Samantamati, and Anantamati.
And with Asamantamati, and Kamalamati, and Mahāmati.
And with Divāmati,
and with Vividhamati,
and with Aśeṣamati.

Honored, revered, worshipped, and adored by Samantabhadra and such leading assemblies of irreversible bodhisattva-mahāsattvas— boundless and limitless— he, the Great Brahmā, sat upon a lotus throne in the midst of the great assembly of followers.

Immediately upon entering the samādhi named *Sarvadurgatipariśodhana*, a multitude of light rays belonging to the great bodhisattva named *Apāyatrayasantativimokṣaka*— emerging from and reabsorbing into the circle of hair between his eyebrows— issued forth. By that light, the triple-thousand great thousandfold world system was illuminated.
By that radiance, having liberated all sentient beings from the bonds of mental afflictions and having individually led them to the Nandana grove, they illuminated it on all sides.

Having honored him with clouds of various offerings, circumambulated him a hundred thousand times, and prostrated with their heads at his feet, they sat upon stainless seats before the Blessed One and spoke thus: "O Buddha! O Buddha! How magnificent is the splendor of the Buddha’s Dharma!"
For what reason?
This is our purification of the miserable realms.
And the establishment in the conduct of a bodhisattva.

Then the Lord of Devas, having circumambulated the Blessed One a hundred thousand times and paid homage to him, addressed the Blessed One as follows: "Blessed One, for what reason have they been liberated from all miserable states by the Buddha’s light, the Universal Radiance, and established on the path of liberation? It is marvelous, O Sugata!
The Blessed One said:
O Lord of Gods, this is not surprising for the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, who have well-accumulated immeasurable stores of merit.
O Lord of Gods, the Perfectly Awakened Ones are mines of infinite jewels of qualities.
O Lord of Gods, the immeasurable skillful means of the Perfectly Awakened Ones are fully perfected.
O Lord of Gods, the wisdom accumulated by the Blessed Buddhas is immeasurable.
O Lord of Gods, the vigor of the Buddhas is infinite.
By the Blessed Buddha, infinite beings to be trained have been made into worthy vessels.

The Blessed Buddhas are awakened to incomparable and equal gnosis; the Blessed Ones are endowed with incomparable and equal miraculous power; the Blessed Ones are endowed with incomparable and equal vows. Therefore, O Lord of Gods, the Blessed Buddhas perform the welfare of sentient beings according to their respective vessels.
Just as there is the performance of the welfare of sentient beings according to those to be trained,
so too does the performance of the welfare of sentient beings occur according to their inclinations;
one should know this, and no doubt, suspicion, or disagreement should be entertained regarding this point.
"It is impossible that there should be anyone who is not to be disciplined by a Tathāgata.
Then the Lord of Devas, rising from his own seat and once again performing a vast and great worship of the Blessed One, addressed the Blessed One as follows:

"O Blessed One, O Sugata, inspire in me the eloquence to act for the benefit of all sentient beings, to show them compassion, to provide them refuge, to exercise great mercy toward them, and to fulfill all their aspirations."
"O Blessed One, inspire my eloquence!
Seven days have passed since the death and passing away of the son of the gods named Vimalamaṇiprabha from this Trāyastriṃśa realm of the gods."
"Blessed One, where has he been reborn? Does he experience happiness or suffering? Blessed One, explain this; Sugata, explain it.
The Blessed One said:
"O Lord of Devas, having known that the time has arrived, you shall hear it.
The Lord of Devas said,
"Bhagavān, this is the time."
“This is the occasion, Sugata.
The Blessed One said:

“O Lord of Devas, the son of the gods named Vimalamaṇiprabha, having passed away from here, has been reborn in the great Avīci hell, where he experiences intense and bitter suffering for twelve thousand years.”
Furthermore, one experiences suffering for ten thousand years in the minor hells;
again, having been reborn among animals or hungry ghosts, one experiences suffering for ten thousand years;
and again, having been reborn in border regions, one experiences the state of being deaf, mute, and of indistinct nature for sixty thousand years.
Furthermore, for eighty-four thousand years, he will be afflicted by diseases such as blood disorders, dysentery, and leprosy; despised by many people, utterly abandoned, and born into a low family.
He does not sever the succession of suffering upon suffering, and he also brings harm to others.
He performs various karmic obstructions without interruption and further experiences a succession of mutual sufferings.
Then, indeed, Śakra and all the sons of the gods, having heard this, were bewildered, terrified, and distressed, falling with their faces cast downward.
Rising again, they spoke thus:
"Bhagavān, how is one liberated from that succession of suffering?
Sugata, how is one liberated?"
"By what means, O Blessed One, is one liberated from that mass of suffering?
Grant protection, O Blessed One!
Grant protection, O Sugata!"
The Blessed One said:
"O Lord of Devas, this was spoken by eighty-four koṭis of Buddhas; I too shall speak it—listen!
Then, O Lord of Devas, [he] again [honored] the Blessed One with various kinds of māndārava and mahāmāndārava flowers."

Having honored [the Buddha] with various excellent ornaments such as jeweled crowns, armlets, earrings, necklaces, half-necklaces, and so forth; having circumambulated him hundreds of thousands of times; and having prostrated while gladdening him with cries of "Excellent, Blessed One! Excellent, Sugata!", I address you for the sake of the well-spoken meaning, in order to bring about the welfare and happiness of the world including its gods, and to liberate future beings from the continuity of the miserable states.
Then again, the hosts of gods, headed by Brahmā, spoke thus:

"Excellent, Blessed One! Excellent, Sugata! For it is through this that even those future beings who have merely heard the names [of these mantras] shall attain liberation from the path of the three lower realms."
"Please speak for the sake of those born in the heavenly realm of the gods or in the human world, so that they may attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Then the Blessed One entered the samādhi called Amoghavajrādhiṣṭhāna (The Empowerment of the Unfailing Vajra) in order to empower Śakra, Brahmā, and the other sons of the gods with the heart-essence of all Tathāgatas.
Oṃ vajrādhiṣṭhānasamaye hūṃ!

Having thus entered into meditative absorption and empowered himself with the empowerment of the invincible vajra, he uttered this *tathāgata-hṛdaya* named "The King that Purifies All Evil Destinies":
*oṃ śodhane śodhane sarvapāpaviśodhani śuddhe viśuddhe sarvakarmāvaraṇaviśuddhe svāhā*.
Immediately upon the recitation of this *vidyā*, the evil destinies of all sentient beings were overturned, and all the realms of hell, animals, and hungry ghosts were purified.
Intense sufferings were pacified, and many became happy and joyful.
Furthermore, he spoke this secret heart-mantra:
*Oṃ śodhane śodhane śodhaya sarvāpāyān sarvasattvebhyo hūṃ*. Furthermore, O Lord of Devas, this is the heart of all Tathāgatas.
Oṃ sarvāpāyaviśodhani hūṃ phaṭ!
Furthermore, O Lord of Gods, this is the heart and sub-heart of all the Tathāgatas:
Oṃ trāṭ!
Furthermore, Lord of Gods, this is the Heart-mantra for Purifying All Evil Destinies:
*Hūṃ*.
Furthermore, Lord of Gods, by merely remembering it, even for beings of little merit, this serves to pacify all evil destinies and brings about liberation without effort.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the King who Purifies All Evil Destinies, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha. It is as follows:
Oṃ śodhane śodhane, purifier of all sins, pure, completely pure, purifier of all karmic obscurations, svāhā! This is the root mantra. Oṃ sarvavit, purify all obscurations, destroy them, hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ sarvavid hūṃ / Oṃ sarvavid hrīḥ phaṭ / Oṃ sarvavid aḥ /
Oṃ sarvavit trāṃ trāṭ / Oṃ sarvavid oṃ / Oṃ sarvavid dhīm /
Oṃ sarvavid hūṃ / Oṃ sarvavit krīṃ traṭ / Oṃ sarvavid mahāvajrodbhavadānapāramitāpūje hūṃ /
The mantra of Lāsyā:
Oṃ sarvavid mahāvajrodbhavaśīlapāramitāpūje trāṃ. The mantra of Mālā:
Oṃ, O all-knowing one, born from the great vajra, worship of the perfection of patience! Hrīḥ!
This is the mantra for song.
Oṃ, O all-knowing one, born from the great vajra, worship of the perfection of vigor! Aḥ!
The mantra of Nṛtyā:
Oṃ sarvavit sarvāpāyaviśodhani dhama dhama dhyānapāramitāpūje huṃ huṃ phaṭ. The mantra of Dhūpā:

Oṃ sarvavit sarvadurgatipariśodhane kleśopakleśacchedani puṣpālokini prajñāpāramitāpūje trāṃ hūṃ phaṭ. This is the mantra for the flower offering. Oṃ sarvavit sarvāpāyaviśodhani jñānālokakari praṇidhipāramitāpūje hrīḥ hūṃ phaṭ.
The mantra of Dīpā:
Oṃ sarvavit sarvāpāyagandhanāśani vajragandhopāyapāramitāpūje aḥ hūṃ phaṭ. The mantra of Gandhā:
Oṃ sarvavid narakagatyākarṣaṇi hūṃ jaḥ phaṭ. This is the mantra of Vajrāṅkuśa. Oṃ sarvavid narakoddharaṇi hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ.
The mantra of Vajrapāśa:
Oṃ sarvavit sarvāpāyabandhanamocani hūṃ vaṃ phaṭ. The mantra of Vajrasphoṭa:
Oṃ sarvavit sarvāpāyagatigahanaviśodhani hūṃ hoḥ phaṭ. This is the mantra of Vajrāveśa. Oṃ maitrīyaharaṇāya svāhā.
The mantra of Maitreya:
Oṃ amoghe amoghadarśini hūṃ.
[This is] of Amoghadarśin.
Oṃ, you who destroy all miserable states, you who purify all miserable states, hūṃ!
[This is] the mantra of Sarvāpāyajaha.
Oṃ, O you whose intellect destroys all sorrow and darkness, hūṃ! [Hail] to the one whose intellect destroys all sorrow and darkness! Oṃ, O Gandhahastinī, hūṃ!
Of the Gandhahastins:
Oṃ śūraṃgame hūṃ!
[This is] of Śūraṃgama.
Oṃ, O sky, O sky-eyed one, hūṃ!
Of Gaganagañja. Oṃ, O banner of wisdom, O possessor of wisdom, hūṃ!
Of Jñānaketu: Oṃ amṛtaprabhe amṛtavati hūṃ.
Of Amṛtaprabha.
Oṃ, you who abide in the moon, you who gaze upon the moon, svāhā!
[This is] for Candraprabha.
Oṃ, auspicious one, protector of the auspicious!
Of Bhadrapāla:
Oṃ jālini mahājālini hūṃ. Of Jālinīprabha:
Oṃ vajragarbhe hūṃ / [for] Vajragarbha. Oṃ akṣaye hūṃ hūṃ, purifier of inexhaustible karmic obscurations, svāhā!
Of Akṣayamati: Oṃ pratibhāne pratibhānakūṭe svāhā.
[This is] of Pratibhānakūṭa.
Oṃ samantabhadre hūṃ!
[This is] of Samantabhadra.
One should recite these mantras of the Bodhisattva of the Fortunate Aeon (Bhadrakalpika) in their proper order.

Following this sequence according to the aforementioned tantra and its prescribed ritual, one should daily practice meditation during the time of dawn through the stage of generation (*utpattikrama*).
By diligently cultivating the deity yoga—the supreme threefold meditative absorption (*samādhi*)—the accomplishment of purifying all miserable rebirths (*durgati*) will be attained.
Furthermore, O Lord of Devas, this is the secret heart-mantra (*guhyahṛdaya*) of the Tathāgata Sarvadurgatipariśodhanatejorāja.

Any son of good family or daughter of good family who hears or retains even the mere name, recites it, or having written it down, wears it bound upon the head, the topknot, the arm, or the neck— such a person, in this very life, shall avoid the eight types of untimely death associated with the manner of dying, as well as those occurring in dreams.
Or whatever signs of an evil rebirth there may be, none of them will approach them except as a mere dream.

Having entered the maṇḍala according to the rules, been consecrated, and having recited the heart-mantra, for those who meditate upon the meaning of the mantra, what need is there to mention that no sins whatsoever shall draw near to them?
They do not go to an evil rebirth.

When anyone— be they men, women, gods, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, pretas, animals, hell-beings, or others— has been initiated after being led into the maṇḍala with their deceased bodies, they are immediately liberated from those hells upon rebirth; having been born among the hosts of gods,
they bring the *dharmatā* of all the Tathāgatas before them and become irreversible.
Their continuity becomes fixed;
they are born into the family of all Tathāgatas,
and their obscurations are abandoned.
In all the families of the Tathāgatas, or in the families of gods, or elsewhere, they experience happiness.
O Lord of Gods, in brief, they experience all mundane and supramundane benefit and happiness.
Then the Lord of Gods, having circumambulated the Blessed One three times as before and having prostrated, spoke thus:

"Blessed One, please teach the Dharma for the sake of bringing benefit and happiness to those who have fallen under the power of all miserable destinies, so that sentient beings may turn their backs on all miserable destinies and effortlessly attain unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

Then, the Blessed One Śākyamuni entered the meditative absorption named *Sarvadurgatipariśodhanajñānavajra* (The Vajra of Wisdom that Purifies All Miserable Destinies) and [manifested] the maṇḍala named *Sarvatathāgatasarvadurgatipariśodhanatejorāja* (The King of Splendor that Purifies All Miserable Destinies of All Tathāgatas).
He spoke:
"The means for accomplishing that was taught by the Lord of the Śākyas.
First of all, the yogin, seated on a soft and comfortable seat in a secluded place agreeable to the mind, should prepare a mandala with fragrant substances and perform the fivefold offering."
Then, having meditated upon the selflessness of all phenomena, one should visualize oneself as a vajra-flame blazing like the sun through the syllable *hūṃ*.

At his throat, by means of the syllable *hrīḥ*, there is a lotus; above that, at the tip of a petal, is a moon mandala by means of the syllable *ā*; and above that, by means of the syllable *hūṃ*, is a five-pronged vajra.
That vajra melts upon the tongue; thus it is called "vajra-tongue. By means of that, one becomes Vajrajihvā.
One becomes capable of reciting the mantra.
In the center of both hands, there is a moon mandala in the form of the letter *si*; above that, by means of the syllable *hūṃ*, there is a five-pronged vajra.
That vajra dissolves into the middle of the hands, and one becomes "Vajrahasta" (Vajra-in-hand).
One shall become capable of binding all mudrās;
thereafter, the meditation on the protection wheel should be performed.
Saying "Oṃ gṛhṇa vajrasamaye hūṃ vaṃ," one should bind the *krodhaterintirī* mudrā;
having placed the vajra-bind at the palms, one should cover [the head] with a mind full of wrath.
Firmly [pressed] with the vajra of the thumb, it is known as Krodhaterintī.
Then, seated upon the half-vajra throne and having bound the *vajra-terintirī* [mudrā], one should receive the vajra-garland initiation with the mantra:
*oṃ vajrajvālānalārka hūṃ abhiṣiñca mām*.
One should hold the two thumbs joined and raised in the *vajra-bandha*, placed in contact upon the *vajra-bandha* [mudrā].
"Vajraterintirī / Oṃ ṭuṃ. Having armored oneself with this two-syllable armor (*kavaca*), one should utter: "Oṃ vajrajvālānalārka hūṃ."
Placing the left vajra-fist at the heart and brandishing the right vajra-fist, one should strike down all obstacles.
Then, with the Vajrānala mudrā, one should perform the burning of obstacles and other rites.
OṂ VAJRĀNALA HANA DAHA PACA MATHA BHAÑJA RANA HUṂ PHAṬ.
Thus one should utter [the mantra].
With the inner vajra-bind (*abhyantaravajrabandha*) and the flames within the fingers, the vajra of the thumbs is raised; this is the Vajrānala-mudrā.
Thereafter: "O Vajranetrī, bind all obstacles! (*vajranetri bandha sarvavighnān*).
One should perform the binding of all obstacles through the application of mudrā.
Having formed the vajra-bind, one should extend both thumbs and hold them level;
this is the Vajranetrī-mudrā.
Having placed the extended vajra-bind upon the ground, one should perform the lower binding with the mantra:
*oṃ vajra dṛḍho me bhava rakṣa sarvān svāhā*. One should then perform the upper binding with the Vajrabhairavanetra mudrā together with its accompanying gesture.
Oṃ hulu hulu huṃ phaṭ.
Having formed two vajra-fists and whirled them like a circle of fire, one should hold them above the head with the index fingers in the shape of hooks.
This is the Vajrabhairava Eye Mudrā.
Below that, one should again perform the binding with Vajrayakṣa together with his mudrā:
Oṃ vajrayakṣa hūṃ.
With the two thumbs extended from the vajrāñjali and the two index fingers forming fangs,
this is the Vajrayakṣa mudrā.
With the Vajroṣṇīṣa mudrā joined, one should bind the eastern direction.

Oṃ druṃ bandha haṃ, or simply "druṃ. Forming two vajra-fists with the little fingers linked like a chain, one should place the tips of the two index fingers like needles upon the crown of the head, turned inward;
this is the Vajroṣṇīṣa mudrā.
Furthermore, one should bind her with the Vajrapāśa [mudrā] using the mantra:
*huṃ vajrapāśe hrīḥ*.
One should form the arm-knot with both vajra-fists.
The Vajrapāśa mudrā. With the Vajrapatākā, one should bind the western direction: Oṃ vajrapatāke pataṅgiṇi raṭa!
Having formed the *vajrabandha* with the thumbs in the *sattvaparyaṅka* posture and the index fingers as needles, with the tips of the ring fingers and little fingers separated,
this is the *vajrapatākā* [mudrā].
One should perform the severing of obstacles in the cardinal and intermediate directions, below, and above.
One should bind the northern direction with Vajrakālī:
*hrīḥ vajrakāli ruṭ maṭ*.
Having firmly placed the Vajrayakṣa mudrā at the mouth of Vajrakālī,
one should bind the southern direction with the Vajraśikhara [mudrā]:
Oṃ vajraśikhare ruṭ maṭ.
Thus,
with the two vajra-fists in the gesture of lifting up a mountain, this is for Vajraśikharā.
Having performed the binding of the maṇḍala by means of Vajrakarma, one should provide the enclosure wall.

"Hūṃ Vajrakarma! Again, with the Vajra-hūṃkāra mantra, "Hūṃ," one should form two vajra-fists, join the arms as a vajra, and extend the two index fingers— which are bound like hooks of the little fingers— as the "Victor over the Three Worlds" (Trilokavijaya) tarjanīs.
This very [gesture], with the two tips joined at the center, is the vajra of Vajrahūṃkāra; it is the vajra of Vajrakarman.
Then, with the Vajracakra mudrā, one should manifest the Sarvadurgatipariśodhana maṇḍala in front, reciting:
*oṃ vajracakra hūṃ*.
Having formed two vajra-fists, one binds them by joining the tips of the two outer fingers.
Renowned as Vajracakrā, she is the accomplisher of all maṇḍalas.
Having rotated this [mantra] clockwise in all directions, the manifestation of the entire mandala occurs.
Placing this very [mantra] upon one's face and gazing [within], one should recite the Vajracakra eight times.

Then, having mentally perceived the mandala as if it were directly present and honored it with flowers and other offerings, one should prostrate toward all directions with the five-pointed salutation (*pañcamaṇḍalaka*) using this [mantra].
"Oṃ, through the prostration of body, speech, and mind to the All-Knowing One, I perform the vajra-binding.
Then, one should perform the four prostrations as follows:
with the entire body and the vajra-añjali extended, one should prostrate toward the eastern direction with this [mantra].
"Oṃ, I offer myself for the service and worship of the All-Knowing One;
O Vajrasattva of all Tathāgatas, please empower me!
Then, rising in the same manner, placing the vajra-añjali at the heart, and touching the ground with the forehead toward the southern direction, one should prostrate with this [mantra].
"Oṃ, O All-Knowing One, I offer myself for the consecration of worship;
consecrate me with the vajra-jewel of all the Tathāgatas.
Then, having likewise arisen, one should prostrate toward the western direction with the vajrāñjali mudrā bound upon the head, touching the ground with the face, while reciting this:
"Oṃ, O Omniscient One, I offer myself for the sake of setting in motion the worship;
O Vajradharma of all Tathāgatas, set me in motion!

Then, having risen in that same manner and lowered the vajra-añjali from his head to his heart, he should prostrate toward the northern direction, touching the ground with his forehead, with this [mantra].
"Oṃ, O All-Knowing One, through this act of worship, I offer myself;

perform for me the vajra-activity of all the Tathāgatas. Having thus spoken, and having placed both knees upon the ground and joined his palms in the vajra-añjali gesture at his heart, he should confess all his misdeeds.

May all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas in the ten directions, as well as all the deities of the mudrās, mantras, and vidyās abiding within the families of the Tathāgata, Vajra, Maṇi, Padma, and Karma, attend to me! I, [name]vajra, [before] all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas in the ten directions...
In the presence of all the Tathāgatas abiding in the families of Vajra, Maṇi, Padma, and Karma, and in the presence of all the mudrās, mantras, vidyās, and deities, I confess all my misdeeds.

In detail, before all the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Pratyekabuddhas, noble Śrāvakas, those who have gone rightly, and those who have practiced rightly throughout the ten directions— past, future, and present— and before all classes of sentient beings...
And I rejoice in all merit;
I entreat all the Blessed Buddhas in the ten directions who have not yet turned the wheel of Dharma to turn the wheel of Dharma.
One should entreat all the Blessed Buddhas in the ten directions who desire to enter final nirvāṇa, requesting them not to pass into final nirvāṇa.
Then, having formed the flower mudrā, one should speak thus:
"Oṃ sarvavit puṣpapūjāmeghasamudraspharaṇasamaye hūṃ."
Having formed the incense mudrā, one should speak thus:
*oṃ sarvavid dhūpapūjāmeghasamudraspharaṇasamaye hūṃ*. Having formed the lamp mudrā, one should speak thus.
Oṃ sarvavid ālokapūjāmeghasamudraspharaṇasamaye hūṃ. Having formed the fragrance mudrā, one should speak thus: Oṃ sarvavid gandhapūjāmeghasamudraspharaṇasamaye hūṃ.
Having formed the *saṃpuṭa-añjali* mudrā, one should speak thus:
*oṃ sarvavid bodhyaṅgaratnālaṃkārapūjāmeghasamudraspharaṇasamaye hūṃ*.
And: *oṃ sarvavid hāsyalāsyaratikrīḍāsaukhyānuttarapūjāmeghasamudraspharaṇasamaye hūṃ*.

Oṃ, at the time of the pervasive ocean-like cloud of supreme cloth-offerings for the All-Knowing One, hūṃ. Then, recollecting the suffering of saṃsāra for all sentient beings, one should bind the action-seal (*karmamudrā*) of the Blessed Lord Vajrasattva and, through the power of compassion, generate the thought of awakening (*bodhicitta*) in order to deliver all sentient beings.

"For the sake of crossing over those who have not crossed, for the sake of liberating those who are unliberated, for the sake of consoling those who are unconsoled, for the sake of bringing to final nirvana those who have not reached it, and for the sake of ferrying the entire realm of sentient beings out of the ocean of saṃsāra:
Oṃ sarvavid vajrapūjāmeghasamudraspharaṇasamaye hūṃ! Then, having formed the *lāsya* mudrā, one should speak thus:
May all sentient beings be endowed with all requisites;
may they possess every perfection dependent upon mere wish.
Oṃ, O All-Knowing One, arising from the Great Vajra, at the time of the pervasive ocean-like cloud of offerings of the perfection of generosity, hūṃ! Thus.
Having bound the Vajramālā mudrā, one should speak thus:
"May all sentient beings be free from all unwholesome actions of body, speech, and mind;
may they be endowed with all wholesome actions of body, speech, and mind."
Oṃ, at the time of the pervasion of the ocean-like clouds of worship consisting of the perfection of morality that nourishes unsurpassed great awakening, O Omniscient One, hūṃ!
Having thus bound the mudrā of song, one should say:
"May all sentient beings have their bodies adorned with all the primary and secondary marks!"
Constantly established in mutual fearlessness and non-hostility toward one another, pleasing to the heart and eyes, and possessing patience regarding the profound Dharma:

Having emerged from the heart, the Instructor should sit down.
Divine, with the luster of a ruby, he is established in the meditation mudrā.
Oṃ Viśvottama Aḥ;
one should emit [it] upon a moon-maṇḍala above a lotus situated on a spoke of the wheel in the north.
Having descended from the heart, the Buddha Viśvoṣṇīṣa, the Tathāgata, [appears].
Blazing with green-colored light, his mudrā is the bestower of fearlessness.
The Buddha, the creator of all works, shall deliver sentient beings from cyclic existence.
With the syllable Oṃ, the Buddha, the Tathāgata Tejoṣṇīṣa, should release [it].
He is properly situated on the eastern spoke, upon a lunar disc resting on a lotus.
Holding the sun with the right hand, he stands with his left hand placed on his hip.
Having the appearance of the colors white and red, he illuminates the three realms.
The Tathāgata Dhvajauṣṇīṣa is born from the seed-syllable HŪṂ.
Having passed beyond the heart, one who is seated on the western spoke should cast it forth.
And upon a moon disc situated on a lotus, he has a reddish-black complexion.
Holding the Cintāmaṇidhvaja, he is the purifier of the stinginess of sentient beings.
The Tathāgata Tīkṣṇoṣṇīṣa is produced from the seed-syllable *dhīḥ*.
Having completely severed the primary and secondary afflictions, one should cast them away upon the spoke of Vāyu.
And he should sit upon a lotus moon; his mudrā has a sword in the right hand.
His body has the color of the sky, and he holds a book in his left hand.
The Tathāgata Chatroṣṇīṣa is born from the seed-syllable *krīṃ*.
And as the Lord of Dharma for all beings, he should release [them] upon the circle of Īśāna.
Resembling the color of jasmine or a white conch shell, this is the mudrā of the one who holds the parasol.
All of them are seated upon lunar discs, resting on universal lotuses.
Having uttered that mantra— *huṃ trāṃ hrīḥ aḥ*— they emit [it] from the heart.
In the four corner positions, upon moon-maṇḍalas situated on lotuses, [one should place the deities].
The four goddesses, Lāsya and the others, bear the colors of their respective families.
White, yellow, red, and multicolored.
Their mudrās are prescribed according to what has been stated.
Having uttered that very mantra, one should release it even from the heart.
The four goddesses, Dhūpā and the others, [are situated] upon moon-mandalas resting on lotuses.
In all four corners, however, according to the sequence of the families of colors.
Oṃ, O you who are pure in all conditioned phenomena, O nature of reality, risen like the sky, pure by intrinsic nature, surrounded by the Great Vehicle, svāhā!
With this mantra, one should dismiss those standing on both sides of the eastern gate.
For the quartet beginning with Maitreya, [the seats are] moon mandalas resting upon lotuses.
All of them are seated upon beings, according to the sequence of their mudrās and colors.
The divine one, possessing yellow-colored radiance, holds a nāgapuṣpa flower in his right hand.
Holding a water-pot in his left hand, through the purity of a mind of loving-kindness.
The second, however, is Amoghadarśin, blazing with a yellow-colored radiance.
With his left hand resting on his hip, he has a lotus in his right eye.
And the third Bodhisattva was named Apāyajaha.
Blazing with white-colored radiance, they hold the goad as their mudrā.
The fourth was Sarvaśokatamonirghātanamati Tathāgata.
They have a complexion appearing as a mixture of white and yellow, and they hold staffs as their hand-symbols.
With his left fist placed upon his hip, he stands in the sattvaparyaṅka posture.
And four bodhisattvas are stationed at the southern gate.
The first is Gandhahastin, and the second is Varṇaka, who is white and dark-blue in color.
This mudrā consists of the right hand holding a scent-conch filled [with perfume].
With his left hand resting on his hip, he is the purifier of all obscurations.
The second is named Śūraṅgama, which liberates one from all afflictions.
This divine seal of the wielder of the sword possesses a radiance with the color of crystal.
With his left hand resting on his hip, he pacifies the suffering of sentient beings.
The third is Gaganagañja, adorned with all ornaments.
He has a radiance of mixed white and yellow colors and is free from all obscurations.
This is the mudrā [of the deity] who holds in his right hand a Dharma-treasury resting upon a lotus.
With his left hand resting on his hip, he holds the treasury of all space.
The fourth is Jñānaketu, who fulfills all aspirations.
Resembling the color of blue sapphire, he holds a wish-fulfilling jewel on his banner.
With his left fist placed upon his hip, he is the liberator from the suffering of poverty.
Seated at the western gate upon a moon disc resting on a lotus.
First is Amṛtaprabha, resplendent with the color of the moon.
Holding a jar of nectar and a crown with his jewel-adorned hand.
With the left fist placed on the hip, it is wide and bestows long life.
The second was named Candraprabha, the destroyer of the darkness of ignorance.
The divine one, whose body is white in color, [displays] a mudrā with his right hand.
With his left fist resting on his hip, he holds a moon disc situated upon a lotus.
The third is Bhadrapāla, whose complexion is white and red.
The mudrā that illuminates all phenomena is formed with the right hand.
Holding a blazing jewel in his left fist, he stands with it placed at his hip.
And the fourth Bodhisattva was named Jālinīprabha.
Divine beings with red-colored radiance, who maintain a vajra-fence.
But the first son of the Buddha is known by the name Vajragarbha.
Endowed with white and blue colors, he holds a mudrā with his right hand.
Holding an utpala flower joined with a vajra, he stands with his left fist placed at his hip.
The second is named Akṣaya (Inexhaustible), whose intellect is established at the limits.
Resembling the color of jasmine and a conch shell, he holds two hand-seals with his two hands.
Holding the flask of wisdom, one should cause all sentient beings to be fully nourished.
And the third son of the Buddha was named Pratibhākūṭa.
Blazing with a red-colored radiance, he displays a mudrā with his right hand.
With his left fist resting at his hip, he holds a jewel-topped lotus.
And the fourth Bodhisattva is named Samantabhadra.
Resembling the color of gold, he holds a mudrā with his right hand.
Holding a divine cluster of jewels and other objects in his left fist, which rests at his hip.
Thus endowed with such a nature, the Bodhisattvas are compassionate by essence.
The Samādhi named Maṇḍalarājāgra:
Oṃ mune mune mahāmunaye svāhā.
Oṃ, homage to the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, the King who Purifies All Evil Destinies.
It is thus: Oṃ śodhane śodhane, purifier of all sins, pure, perfectly pure, purified of all karmic obscurations, svāhā!
By means of this mantra, one should visualize [the mandala] complete with the thirty-seven deities, headed by the glorious Śākyasiṃharāja.
Thereafter, having opened the door while joined with the mantra and mudrā, one should draw forth the maṇḍala of gnosis.
Having formed two vajra-fists, one should extend the two index fingers.
Having linked the little fingers together with the mudrā for opening the door.
Oṃ, O Omniscient One, open the door! Hūṃ.
With the mantra and mudrā for opening the door, one should open the door.
With the Vajracakra-mudrā, one should visualize the maṇḍala.
Oṃ sarvavid vajracakre hūṃ!
[This is for] the release of the vajra-clap by means of the vajra-bind with both arms.
The glorious Śākyarāja, whose nature is yoga, shall assemble all the Buddhas.
With the chaṭaka rhythm on the left and the sama rhythm, it is accomplished.
But by means of the southern [wind], both types of morbid humors (saṃnipāta) mentioned by Tāla are [cured].
Oṃ vajrasamāja jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ!
By the mere power of this command, [may] the entire assembly of the circle of deities with their retinues [be summoned].
All the Buddhas come together; what need is there to mention others?

Then, having visualized the mandala circle in the space before him, he should sprinkle it with scented water contained in the argha vessel over which the Vajrayakṣa mantra has been recited, and offer water for rinsing the mouth (ācamana).
Then, he should offer the argha with the argha-mudrā.
Then, one should offer the water for the feet with the *pādya* mudrā. Then:
*vajrapuṣpe hūṃ*;
*vajradhūpe hūṃ*.
With "Vajradīpe hūṃ" and "Vajragandhe hūṃ," having dispelled the obstacles by means of the Vajrayakṣa mantra, one should cause them to enter the maṇḍalas.
Then follow the four mudrās.
First, one should bind the samaya-mudrā by means of the previously mentioned vidhi-mudrā.
Then, the Dharma-mudrā is performed with the previously mentioned mantra.
Then, one should bind the Karma-mudrā with the Karma-mudrā mantra.
Then, one should bind the Mahāmudrā with the Mahāmudrā mantra.

Then, the Tathāgatas beginning with Vajroṣṇīṣa, having emanated Sattvavajrī, Ratnavajrī, Dharmavajrī, and Karmavajrī, should bestow the empowerment upon the deities of the maṇḍala, starting from Śrī Śākyarāja and ending with Vajrāveśa;
they should bestow it up to the status of the Lord of the Five Empowerments.
Immediately after the consecration:
Oṃ, at the time of the pervasive ocean-cloud of incense-offerings of all Tathāgatas, hūṃ!
Oṃ, at the time of the pervasive ocean-cloud of flower-offerings of all Tathāgatas, hūṃ!
Oṃ, at the time of the pervasive ocean-like cloud of lamps for the worship of all Tathāgatas, hūṃ!
Oṃ, at the time of the pervasive ocean-like cloud of perfumes for the worship of all Tathāgatas, hūṃ!
Then, one should perform worship with the four [mudrās] beginning with Lāsyā.
Brandishing the vajra, one should perform praise with the hundred-syllable mantra of Vajravāc as before. Then:
"O you whose nature is the Dharma, which is peerless, immovable, and of supreme essence;
whose very self is compassion, you who remove suffering from the world."
Bestowers of the accomplishment of all qualities without exception.
They are immovable and possess the supreme, peerless dharma.
In the sky, it has reached a state of non-comparison; it is not to be found.
Even a minute particle of the dust of their virtues is boundless.
To those who bestow the supreme accomplishment of the manifest realm of sentient beings.
Among those who are beyond comparison and whose accomplishments are universal.
Constantly stainless, it arises from the impulse of compassion.
The fulfillment of one's vow is the nature of non-cessation.
She is intent on accomplishing the welfare of the world and is skilled in counsel.
It shines perpetually for those whose nature is great compassion.
Those who practice the conduct of compassion do not bring about cessation.
She proceeds, bestowing the supreme accomplishment of the three worlds.
They have reached perfect completion among those who are immeasurable and infinite.
Even when those who have attained a happy rebirth pass away, oh, how wonderful is the nature of reality!
May they, who grant the boon of the supreme accomplishment of the samaya, bestow it upon me.
The state of being a giver of boons has always led to rebirth in the happy realms.
She is the bestower of the supreme accomplishments of all the three worlds.
The state of having gone through the three times as a Sugata is unobstructed.
Everywhere, having resolved upon an offering of praise with a hundred-faced tongue, one holding a vajra-bell should perform the eulogy.

Then, one should present the bali-offering, together with the ritual implements and all types of worship, to all the Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas in the ten directions, as well as to the worldly and transcendent external deities; and one should recite the extensive liturgy many times.
First, one should draw in the heaps of sins with the sound "chaṭa" and so forth.
Accompanied by the Trilokavijaya mudrā and endowed with the three syllables and so forth.
The entire world-system of rebirths in all miserable states, without exception.
Attraction, extraction, binding, and destruction.
There are four well-composed mantras;
with these mantras, beginning with *tāḍya*, while striking white mustard seeds,
the bone, together with a white cloth, should be washed.
One should wash away the impurities of the three worlds with water using the mantra beginning with *oṃ śodhana*.
One should wash it with the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*) using the mantra beginning with *oṃ kaṅkaṇi*.
One should wash it with all types of perfumes using the mantra beginning with *oṃ ratne ratne*.
One should wash [the vessel] with milk using the mantra beginning with *oṃ amoghāvaraṇa*.
One should wash the finest liquor with the mantra beginning with *oṃ amṛte amṛta*.
One should wash it thoroughly inside and out with water using the mantra beginning with *oṃ puṇye puṇya*.
Furthermore, one should have the auspicious verses recited and perform the consecration;
the purification of the path must be carried out,
and the fourfold mantras should be offered with incense and other substances.
This fire-pit should be made one cubit in measure; then one should perform the fire-oblation.
And having recollected that being who is situated in a state of miserable rebirth,
One of auspicious lineage should perform the fire offering for the pacification of sinful obscurations.
With parched grain and mustard seeds mixed with ghee, milk, and honey.
For sesame, rice, paddy, and so forth, as well as for sacrificial fuel sticks, both hands [are used].
However, he should perform other rites as well, just as previously described.
"By that, one quickly attains [success] and brings happiness to sentient beings. Thus ends the *Karmarājāgrī-nāma-samādhi*.
And when that has been performed for the sake of a sentient being, [the result follows].

Then, being liberated from the sufferings of hell, they were born among the Tuṣita gods as benefactors of all sentient beings, appearing like Sugatas. Thereupon, the gods of great renown, together with Indra, danced and offered infinite clouds of worship for the sake of honoring the Tathāgata in this birth.

Placing [the Buddha] at their head, the hosts of gods, having generated the thought of awakening (*bodhicitta*), made the Nandana grove adorned with many forms of divine flowers, incense, lamps, perfumes, parasols, banners, flags, and so forth,
and filled it with rains of garments, jewels, and other offerings.
Then a great marvel occurred.
Then the Blessed One, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, through the empowerment of the Blessed One, proclaimed the subsequent ritual manual for the King of Ritual Manuals of Mantras.
Rising from his heroic posture, exultant and brandishing his vajra, he bowed to the Lord of the Śākyas, the Sovereign of Sages, Nanda.

Entering the meditative absorption named Sarvāvaraṇaviśodhanavajra (Vajra that Purifies All Obstructions), he emitted from his own heart this heart-mantra named Durgatipariśodhana (Purification of Evil Destinies):
Oṃ sarvapāpadahanavajra hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ, vajra that purifies all lower realms, hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ, reduce all karmic obscurations to ashes, hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ bhrūṃ, destroy the obscurations, hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ druṃ, purify the obscurations! Hūṃ phaṭ! Oṃ jvala jvala, burn burn, strike strike the obscurations! Hūṃ phaṭ! Oṃ sruṃ, move move, spread spread the obscurations! Hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ hūṃ hara hara all obscurations hūṃ phaṭ! Oṃ hūṃ phaṭ shatter all obscurations hūṃ phaṭ! Oṃ bhṛta bhṛta all obscurations hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ traṭa traṭa, all obscurations, hūṃ phaṭ! Oṃ chinda chinda, vidrava vidrava, all obscurations, hūṃ phaṭ! Oṃ daha daha, the cause of all rebirths in the hells, hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ paca paca, [burn] the cause of all rebirths as a preta, hūṃ phaṭ! Oṃ matha matha, [churn away] the cause of all rebirths as an animal, hūṃ phaṭ!
Then he spoke of their requisites.
Oṃ, purifier of all sins, cleanse, cleanse, incense, hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ, purifier of all miserable rebirths, beholder of flowers, hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ, purifier of all states of woe, maker of the light of wisdom, hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ, destroyer of all rebirths in the lower realms, gandha hūṃ phaṭ! Oṃ, attractor of those in the hell realm, hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ, deliverer from all rebirths in the hell realm, hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ, liberator from the bonds of all miserable states, hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ, destroyer of the dense thickets of all rebirths in miserable states, hūṃ phaṭ!
Then he spoke of the mandala:
"The mandala is the space between the wheels, beautifully adorned with eight spokes."
It is joined with a hub and a rim, and provided with an inner covering.
Having drawn [the mandala], one should draw the Sage, the Lord of the Śākyas, at the navel.
Then, one should draw Vajrapāṇi of great strength at the forefront of the heroes.
And one should draw the Cakravartin behind [it].
One should draw Jayoṣṇīṣa on the right and Vijaya on the left.
A mass of light in the southeast, and a white parasol in the northeast.
One should draw Vikiriṇa in the northwest and Vidhvaṃsaka in the southwest.
Then, one should draw the exterior:
a square with four gates, adorned with four archways.
The hook, the noose, the chain, and the bell should be established by the Hero.
Flowers and other offerings should be depicted in all the corners.
Then, one should anoint one's own body with garlands, perfumes, incense, and so forth.
In the same manner, the Vajrācārya should enter with:
*jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ*. "O Blessed One, come, O Great Compassionate One, you who are visible! *hoḥ*!"
Thus,
one should summon all the gods.
Having been caused to enter in that same manner and having been consecrated, they are liberated from all miserable rebirths and arise in the heavenly worlds and the supramundane stages.
All accomplishments (*siddhi*) are likewise attained,
and perfect enlightenment (*samyaksaṃbodhi*) is necessarily achieved;
they perform all activities as before.
They become unimpeded everywhere;
by means of purification, they liberate [beings] from all fevers, seizures, and the like;
and Vajrapāṇi performs all activities through the syllable *huṃ*.
Even by means of the ritual procedure of another *kalpa*, one becomes a practitioner of all [attainments].

By drawing the images and so forth of gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, rākṣasas, and others who have fallen under the power of miserable rebirths (*durgati*), liberation from all miserable rebirths occurs through recitation, fire-offerings (*homa*), and consecrations (*abhiṣeka*).
Then the Blessed One Vajradhara, having gazed upon the face of the Blessed One with a lion’s look, bowed and spoke this:
"O Blessed One, you have proclaimed the supreme characteristic of the Supreme Mudrā; with a mind overcome by the feeling of compassion, all the Victors bestow their blessing.
Remaining in meditative absorption and joining the palms at the forehead, one should prostrate."
The mudrā for bowing to the Buddhas:
the knower of yoga should form the añjali at the region of the throat in the shape of a closed lotus.
In the Lotus family, there is the lotus mudrā.
Placing the vajra-añjali at the heart, one joins the middle fingers like needles;
this is the *samaya-mudrā* of the Vajra family.
Having placed the left hand palm-upward on the lap and positioned the right hand upon it, one should join the two thumbs and gaze calmly while looking ahead.
This is the samaya of the samādhi-mudrā in the Tathāgata family.
By reversing that very same [mudrā] and joining them with one another, binding the little fingers and thumbs in the form of a chain, one should place it at the heart.
This is the samaya-mudrā in the Vajra family.
Having formed a full *añjali*, one should hold the little fingers and thumbs like needles and extend the remaining fingers;
this is the lotus mudrā (*padmamudrā*) in the Lotus Family.
Having made the *vajrabandha* firm, one should form the middle fingers into a vajra-needle and extend the little fingers and thumbs.
This is the vajra-mudrā of Vajrapāṇi.
Having formed the two little fingers and the thumbs of that very same [mudrā] in the same manner, one should form the index and ring fingers in the shape of lotus petals.
This is the all-purifying mudrā of the King who Purifies All Evil Destinies.
One should form the shape of a jewel with that very ring finger and index finger;
this is the consecration mudrā (*abhiṣeka-mudrā*). Having joined the little fingers and thumbs separately, the remaining fingers are extended.
The *sarvaprasahana-mudrā* is formed by turning the left hand in the same manner. The *sarvakarmika-mudrā* is formed by raising the joined palms upward.
The *dhūpa-mudrā* is formed by tossing the joined palms upward.
By lowering that same [hand] downward, it is the flower mudrā;
that same [hand], in the shape of a conch, is the incense mudrā;
holding that very same [hand] extended outward constitutes the offering mudrā.
From that very same [mudrā], with the two middle fingers joined, it is the *arpaṇa-mudrā*.
Having formed the *vajrabandha* and bent the joints of the two middle fingers while joining them together, one should extend all the other fingers; this is the *vikīrinī-mudrā*.
From that same [mudrā], drawing back the two little fingers and the two thumbs, it is the *vidhvaṃsana-mudrā*.
That same añjali-gesture, shaped like a radiant orb, is the Tejorāśi-mudrā.
Rotating that very same gesture at the location of the uṣṇīṣa is the Sitātapatra-mudrā.
Having bound the two little fingers and thumbs in the form of a chain within the vajrabandha, one should rotate it upward.
The Cakramudrā:

In the Vajrabandha, having formed the middle fingers in the shape of a vajra and the index fingers in the shape of jewels, the remaining fingers are made into the shape of light; this is the Jayoṣṇīṣamudrā.

In the same way, having formed the two index fingers into a vajra and bound the remaining fingers so they take the form of a vajra, one should perform the mudrā of Vijayā. The Tathāgatī [mudrā] grants the boon with the right hand and likewise grants fearlessness with the left.
In the vajrabandha, one should form the two index fingers into the shape of a vajra; this is the vajramudrā.
This very [hand], with the right index finger drawn out like a hook, is the *Aṅkuśī*;
that same [hand] in the form of a spear is the *Śara*;
and that same [hand] with the thumb placed at the tip is for one of virtuous mind (*Sādhumati*).
That very [finger] broken in the middle is the jewel;
its fingers, having the form of light, are the radiance. One should place that very [finger] upon the uṣṇīṣa as the ketu-mudrā.
One should place that very same [mudrā] in front as the vāśa-mudrā; that same [mudrā], when formed in the shape of a lotus, is the padma;
and that same [mudrā], when drawn forward at the tip, is the khaḍga.
One should make that very [line] ring-shaped as the wheel;
that same [line], shaped like a lotus petal, is the tongue;
and that same [line], extended at its tip, is Viśvā.
That same [mudrā], when well extended, is the protection; that same one, when slightly contracted at the front, is the yakṣa;
that same one, when not contracted, is the binding.
Of that same [mudrā], the two index fingers bent [inward] form the hook (aṅkuśa); that same [mudrā] with the tips grasped together forms the noose (pāśa);
and that same [mudrā] with the fingers interlaced forms the thunderbolt (sphoṭa).
And he moved it out of satisfaction.

Then the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi, having looked upon that great circle of the assembly headed by Śakra and Brahmā, and having gratified them with words of approval, said: "Excellent, excellent, O sons of the gods headed by Śakra, that you possess such eloquence!"
"That which has arisen is excellent; practice it, for I shall teach it.

Then the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi entered the samādhi called "The Vajra Arising from the Pervasion of All Amitāyus," [and revealed] the heart-mantra of all Tathāgatas called "The Increaser of the Accumulations of Immeasurable Life, Merit, and Wisdom."
It issued forth from his own heart:
*Oṃ puṇye puṇye mahāpuṇye aparimitapuṇye aparimitāyuḥpuṇyajñānasaṃbhāropacayakāriṇi svāhā*.

As soon as this *Sarvatathāgatahṛdayadhāraṇī* was spoken, all states of woe were pacified, and all beings fallen into the realms of hell, hungry ghosts, and animals were liberated and attained self-awareness.
All world-systems were illuminated; having been illuminated, they performed the twelvefold activity of a Buddha and then entered back into those very syllables of the Dharma-heart of all Tathāgatas.
Then, the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called Amitāyur-vajraprabhākarī and spoke this heart-dhāraṇī called Sarvatathāgatāyur-vajra:
Oṃ amṛte amṛte amṛtodbhave amṛtasaṃbhave amṛtavikrāntagāmini sarvakleśakṣayaṃkari svāhā!
Then, as soon as this was spoken, all the sufferings of all sentient beings were pacified in that very way.

Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called *Amoghāvaraṇavināśanī* (The Destruction of Fruitless Obstructions) and emitted from his own heart this heart-essence dhāraṇī called *Sarvatathāgatāvaraṇatroṭana* (The Severing of the Obstructions of All Tathāgatas):
*oṃ kaṃkaṇi kaṃkaṇi rocani rocani troṭani troṭani pratihana pratihana sarvakarmaparaṃparāṇi sarvasattvānāṃ svāhā*.
As soon as this was spoken, everything became exactly so.

Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called Sarvāvaraṇavimalaviśuddhivajra (the Vajra of Purity Free from All Obscurations) and emitted from his own heart this heart-dhāraṇī called Sarvatathāgatāśeṣāvaraṇavināśanī (the Destroyer of All Remaining Obscurations of All Tathāgatas).
Oṃ ratne ratne mahāratne ratnasaṃbhave ratnakiraṇe ratnamālāviśuddhe śodhaya sarvapāpaṃ hūṃ phaṭ! As soon as this was spoken, all the abodes of Māra were shattered and utterly destroyed.

Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi named *Amoghāpratihatasarvāvaraṇavidhvaṃsana* (The Destruction of All Obstructions, Unfailing and Unimpeded), and from his own heart he uttered this *dhāraṇī* of the heart of all Tathāgatas:
*Oṃ amoghāpratihatasarvāvaraṇavināśani hara hara huṃ phaṭ*.
As soon as this was spoken, the entire world-system of analogies shook, trembled, and quaked; it moved, swayed, and vibrated; it was agitated, stirred, and tossed about.
Many wonders and marvels were seen in the world;
